title: bug: the JetBrains plugin treats the IDE's LightEdit pseudo-project as a Moe project: projectOpened registers it in ~/.moe/projects.json, scaffolds .moe/ into the IDE config folder (<config>/light-edit) and spawns a daemon for it, so opening a single file or an unrecognised folder in LightEdit starts a stray Moe daemon (PyCharm 2026.1, 2026-11-02 10:52: port 9877, pid 37792)
description:
Filed by the governor (governor-e6142a94) on 2026-11-04 from hunt #21's held-back item (a) (task-e5d38de9, architect-2a219562, #governors msg-74156a8d). The draft is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-e5d38de9/mine/lightedit-row-draft.md, and the evidence is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-e5d38de9/mine/lightedit-evidence.txt. The governor re-verified the code citation at origin/moe/work-2026-10-24 and the on-disk state on 11-04.

PROBLEM
- moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/listeners/MoeProjectOpenListener.kt:11-16 runs for every opened project: `MoeProjectRegistry.registerProject(basePath, project.name)`, then `project.service<MoeProjectService>().connect()`.
- connect() (MoeProjectService.kt:140-161) calls daemonSupervisor.ensureMoeInitialized(). That scaffolds .moe/ when it is missing (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:654-665, MoeProjectInitializer.initializeProject), then calls ensureDaemonRunning(), which spawns a daemon.
- Nothing checks LightEdit. `git grep -i lightedit` over moe-jetbrains/src/main at the tip is empty.
- The LightEdit project is the IDE's internal single-file editor. Its basePath is the IDE config folder (C:/Users/<u>/AppData/Roaming/JetBrains/<IDE>/light-edit), not a user project.
- PyCharm falls back to it when a folder will not open as a project. idea.log shows "No processor found for project in D:\projexts\U&AI" right before the start.

EVIDENCE (the user's own IDE)
- idea.log, 2026-11-02 10:52:03-04 local: "Removed stale daemon.json (PID 11892 not reachable or another project)", then "Started Moe daemon for C:/Users/Yaron/AppData/Roaming/JetBrains/PyCharm2026.1/light-edit", then the daemon listening on port 9877.
- ~/.moe/projects.json:13 registers that light-edit path. The entry is named LightEditProject.
- <config>/light-edit/.moe/ exists. Its activity.log and agent-context.md date from 2026-07-13, so this has recurred since July. Its daemon.json is from 2026-11-02 (pid 37792, port 9877).

FIX DIRECTION
- In MoeProjectOpenListener.projectOpened, return early when `LightEdit.owns(project)` (com.intellij.ide.lightEdit.LightEdit). That skips the registry entry, the .moe/ scaffold and the daemon.
- Guard MoeProjectService.connect() too, since the tool window and panels can call it. The same check for WorktreeExclusionListener is optional.
- If the platform call cannot be faked in a unit test, inject a predicate, like the service's other seams.
- Out of scope: cleaning the existing light-edit/.moe/ folder and the projects.json entry. Mention them in the summary as a manual one-off.

SCOPE AND CHECKS
- MoeProjectOpenListener.kt, MoeProjectService.kt and their tests. At filing time no open row holds them (lanes.js, 09:30Z).
- Gate: `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` on the Windows gate host under the jetbrains-gradle lease.
definitionOfDone: Opening a LightEdit project neither registers it in ~/.moe/projects.json, creates .moe/, nor starts a daemon. A JUnit test pins the guard and fails without it.
A normal project still registers, scaffolds and starts its daemon as before, and the existing tests stay green.
`./gradlew test` passes on the gate host under the jetbrains-gradle lease.

implementationPlan.description:
Listener guard and its test (DoD 1, DoD 2).

CHANGE. In MoeProjectOpenListener.projectOpened (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/listeners/MoeProjectOpenListener.kt:11-16), make the first statement `if (LightEdit.owns(project)) return`, with the import com.intellij.ide.lightEdit.LightEdit. Add a one-line comment: the IDE's LightEdit pseudo-project (basePath = <IDE config>/light-edit) is not a Moe project, so it gets no registry entry, no .moe/ scaffold and no daemon.
- Error handling: the guard is a pure instanceof check that cannot throw, and it adds no new failure path.
- A non-LightEdit project keeps the existing `basePath ?: return` early exit and everything after it.

API FACTS (verified with javap on the gradle-cached SDK idea-2026.2.3-win):
- `public static boolean owns(Project)` in lib/intellij.platform.editor.ui.jar is exactly `aload_0; instanceof com.intellij.ide.lightEdit.LightEditCompatible; ireturn`.
- LightEditCompatible (lib/intellij.platform.core.jar) is an empty marker interface.
- LightEdit has only a private constructor plus owns: no static initializer and no @ApiStatus annotation.
- So no predicate seam is needed. A test Proxy that implements both Project and LightEditCompatible makes the REAL LightEdit.owns return true, headless.

TEST. New file moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/listeners/MoeProjectOpenListenerTest.kt, JUnit 4 like the rest of src/test.
- Build the Proxy projects the way MoeProjectServiceTest.kt:49-80 does (fakeProject + defaultReturn), parameterised by basePath, the extra LightEditCompatible interface, and what getService(Class) returns.
- Isolate the registry. MoeProjectRegistry reads System.getProperty("user.home") on every call (MoeProjectRegistry.kt:30). Point user.home at a temp dir for each test, and as error handling for a failing assertion restore the previous value in a finally block (or @After). Then delete the temp dirs. Without this, a RED run on the gate host writes the developer's real ~/.moe/projects.json.
- Case A (LightEdit). The Proxy implements Project + LightEditCompatible, basePath = a temp dir, and getService records any call. `MoeProjectOpenListener().projectOpened(project)` must throw nothing and never call getService, and must leave <tempHome>/.moe/projects.json and <tempBase>/.moe absent.
  - Without the guard, registerProject writes the registry first, then the `project.service<MoeProjectService>()` lookup gets null and throws. The case therefore fails before any connect could scaffold or spawn.
- Case B (normal project, the control). The Proxy implements Project only, basePath = a temp dir, and getService(MoeProjectService::class.java) returns `MoeProjectService(<a Proxy project with basePath null>) { it() }`.
  - projectOpened must create <tempHome>/.moe/projects.json containing the temp basePath; read it back. This proves normal projects still register.
  - That service's connect() stops at ensureMoeInitialized (blank basePath → false, MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:655), so nothing is scaffolded or spawned. Dispose the service at the end.

OUT OF SCOPE. Do not touch WorktreeExclusionListener (util/WorktreeExclusion.kt:175): it only edits module roots, and a LightEdit project has none.

connect() guard and its tests (DoD 1, DoD 2).

CHANGE. In MoeProjectService.connect() (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectService.kt:140), change the first line to `if (disposed.get() || LightEdit.owns(project)) return`, importing com.intellij.ide.lightEdit.LightEdit.
- The check runs BEFORE the wsLock check-and-set. A LightEdit project therefore never sets `connecting`, publishes no status, and never reaches daemonSupervisor.ensureMoeInitialized() or ensureDaemonRunning().
- ensureMoeInitialized() is the .moe/ scaffold: MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:654-665 calls MoeProjectInitializer.initializeProject, which also calls registerProject at MoeProjectInitializer.kt:95.
- Error handling is unchanged for every other project: ensureMoeInitialized's catch and "Project not initialized" status, the stale daemon.json clean-up and the reconnect scheduling all stay as they are.
- Every automatic path funnels through connect(): the open listener, the tool window panel's init (MoeToolWindowPanel.kt:362) and the reconnect/retry paths.
- InitMoeAction and the panel's Init (MoeToolWindowPanel.kt:822-828) are explicit user actions on a chosen folder. Leave them.

TESTS. In moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectServiceTest.kt, beside the existing cases. Use the same synchronous invokeLaterForTests lambda and MoeStateListener status collector as `manual disconnect publishes disconnected status immediately`.
- Add a lightEditProject() helper: the existing fakeProject() Proxy with LightEditCompatible added to its interfaces. basePath stays null.
- Case C: `MoeProjectService(lightEditProject()) { it() }`, then connect(). statuses must equal emptyList() and isConnected() must be false. Without the guard it publishes `false to "Project not initialized"`, so the case fails.
- Case D (control): `MoeProjectService(fakeProject()) { it() }`, then connect(). statuses must equal listOf(false to "Project not initialized").
- basePath stays null in both cases on purpose. A blank basePath makes ensureMoeInitialized() return false before any scaffold or spawn (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:655). So neither a GREEN run nor a RED run with the guard removed can create .moe/, write ~/.moe/projects.json or start a daemon on the gate host.
- Dispose each service in a finally block.

Verification gate, run ONCE (DoD 1, DoD 3). JetBrains gradle from WSL, per mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-from-wsl.

1. Take the lease with moe.acquire_resource { resourceId: "jetbrains-gradle" }. Release it with moe.release_resource when done, whether the run passes or fails.
2. Run from this task's worktree (worktree mode: D:\projexts\moes\.worktrees\<taskId>). From bash, single-quote the whole cmd string and leave the --tests filters unquoted.
   - RED/GREEN: temporarily remove the two guards and run `cmd.exe /d /c 'set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d <worktree>\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --tests com.moe.listeners.MoeProjectOpenListenerTest --tests com.moe.services.MoeProjectServiceTest --rerun'`. Cases A and C must fail and B and D pass. Restore the guards and rerun: everything passes.
   - Full: `cmd.exe /d /c 'set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d <worktree>\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun'` must end with BUILD SUCCESSFUL.
   - Confirm that :test executed rather than reporting UP-TO-DATE: the fresh build/test-results/test/TEST-com.moe.listeners.MoeProjectOpenListenerTest.xml and TEST-com.moe.services.MoeProjectServiceTest.xml carry the new cases with 0 failures.
3. complete_task evidence: the full Windows command exactly as run, its exit code and the output tail (BUILD SUCCESSFUL plus the test count). Label it as the Windows equivalent of `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test`, not as the POSIX command. Also report the RED run's failing cases.
4. In the summary, name the manual one-off cleanup this row does not do:
   - the existing <IDE config>/light-edit/.moe/ folder (here C:/Users/<u>/AppData/Roaming/JetBrains/PyCharm2026.1/light-edit/.moe);
   - the LightEditProject entry in ~/.moe/projects.json.

Adversarial self-review of this row's diff, as the final step (load adversarial-self-review). Check:
- The guard is the first statement in both entry points, before any registry write, wsLock or `connecting` change, status publish or supervisor call. A normal project's path, including its error handling, is unchanged apart from one instanceof check (cases B and D).
- A second, concurrent connect() on a LightEdit project also returns before the lock, so no flag can stick.
- Every test restores user.home in finally, even when an assertion fails, and deletes its temp dirs. No test can reach a real daemon spawn: both service cases keep basePath null, and the listener's LightEdit case dies at the service lookup when the guard is removed.
- Nothing else in moe-jetbrains/src/main registers, scaffolds or spawns for an opened project without going through these two entry points. Re-grep for `registerProject(`, `ensureMoeInitialized`, `initializeProject(` and `ensureDaemonRunning(`, and list any new caller in the summary.
- The diff touches only the four plan files, and nothing under .moe/ is edited by hand.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Opening the IDE's LightEdit pseudo-project (a single file, or a folder PyCharm cannot open as a project) neither registers it in ~/.moe/projects.json, scaffolds .moe/ into the IDE config folder, nor starts a Moe daemon. Every other project registers, scaffolds and connects exactly as before.
invariants: LightEdit.owns(project) is checked before any MoeProjectRegistry write, wsLock/connecting change, status publish, ensureMoeInitialized() or ensureDaemonRunning() call.
A non-LightEdit project takes the same path as before: registerProject in projectOpened, then connect() unchanged, including its existing error handling.
Tests never write the real ~/.moe/projects.json (user.home points at a temp dir and is restored in finally) and never start a daemon (service cases keep basePath null).
compatibility: No .moe/ state or wire change. Existing projects.json entries, including the stray LightEditProject one, are left as they are; cleanup is manual and out of scope.
sinceBuild 231: com.intellij.ide.lightEdit.LightEdit.owns(Project) is public platform API with no @ApiStatus marker.
reuse: The Proxy fakeProject()/defaultReturn pattern from MoeProjectServiceTest.kt:49-80 and its synchronous invokeLaterForTests lambda plus MoeStateListener collector.
sourceAssumptions: LightEdit.owns(Project) == project instanceof LightEditCompatible (javap, idea-2026.2.3 lib/intellij.platform.editor.ui.jar); LightEditCompatible is an empty marker interface in lib/intellij.platform.core.jar.
MoeDaemonSupervisor.ensureMoeInitialized returns false on a blank basePath before scaffolding (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:654-656).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Inject a LightEdit predicate seam into the listener and the service. Not needed: LightEdit.owns is a plain instanceof against an empty marker interface, so a Proxy that implements LightEditCompatible drives the real check headless. (2) Guard only the listener. Rejected: connect() is public and also runs from the tool window panel and the reconnect/retry paths. (3) Guard inside MoeDaemonSupervisor.ensureMoeInitialized/ensureDaemonRunning. Rejected: the supervisor only gets basePath and projectName, not the Project, and the listener's registry write happens before it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: JetBrains unit tests are JUnit 4, headless, with java.lang.reflect.Proxy projects (MoeProjectServiceTest.kt:49-80); there is no platform fixture. MoeProjectRegistry resolves ~/.moe from user.home on every call. ensureMoeInitialized() bails out on a blank basePath, which is the safe lever that keeps service tests from scaffolding or spawning. `project.service<T>()` is an inline extension that calls getService(Class) on the Proxy and throws when it gets null.
planningNotes.risks: A test that leaks user.home or writes the real registry. A RED run that reaches a real daemon spawn (prevented by keeping basePath null in the service cases, and by the listener case dying at the service lookup). Gradle-from-WSL quoting: single-quote the cmd string and leave --tests unquoted, or gradle prints 'No tests found'. A 5 s BUILD SUCCESSFUL can be UP-TO-DATE: use --rerun and check the TEST-*.xml timestamps.
